title: Investigation: Latency Attribution Workshop Notes
content:
Purpose:
Runbook-style notes from a 2025-11-03 cross-team workshop to converge on a small, high-impact set of signals and dashboards for rapid latency attribution during token-serving incidents. Focus is on quick operator hypotheses, trace anchors, and a minimal dashboard that supports 3-minute hypotheses.

Context and constraints:
- We observed recurring incidents where 90th/99th token-latency spikes correlate with: cold KV cache, multi-model fanout, and per-tenant backpressure.
- Query budget: dashboard queries should run at 1m cadence with <= 10s runtime per panel.
- Privacy: traces for PII-laden prompts need redaction; only include hash/replay-id in traces.

Audience:
- Oncall operators, SREs, serving-runtime engineers, solutions engineers helping customers debug latency.

High-level goals from workshop:
1) Define a compact latency-attribution ladder: origin -> component -> micro-path -> token position.
2) Standardize trace annotations (anchors) so panel links open a focused trace with the right spans highlighted.
3) Create 6 panels that answer the operator's top 3 questions in under 3 minutes.
4) Lightweight probes to detect KV cold starts and model warmup regressions.

Signal taxonomy (prioritized):
- User-perceived latency (UPL): client RTT to first token + server TTF token.
- Server-side token latency quantiles (p50/p90/p99) broken out by model-version and route.
- KV-cache "warmth" index: fraction of requests where prefix-KV hit ratio > 0.7 in the last 10m per pool.
- Fanout depth and branch count: number of parallel model calls for a request (0/1/2+).
- Model queue depth and dequeue latency per GPU-pool.
- Tenant-weighted CPU/GPU contention metric: tenant_cpu_share / pool_share aggregated.
- External dependency latency (embeddings store, prompt-store) 90th.

Metric definitions (operator-facing, canonical names):
- upl.first_token_rtt_ms (histogram) - client->edge->server round-trip to first token arrival.
- server.token_latency_ms (histogram, tags: model, route, tenant, seq_len) - per-token generation latency.
- kv.prefetch_hit_ratio (gauge, tags: pool, model) - rolling 10m fraction of requests with prefix hits.
- fanout.branch_count (gauge, tags: request_id) - integer count of model calls spawned by request.
- pool.queue_latency_ms (summary, tags: pool_id) - time spent waiting before being dispatched to GPU.
- tenant.resource_pressure_score (gauge) - heuristic 0..1 combining batch wait, retries, throttles.

Tracing conventions (minimal, enforceable):
- Root span: request_id = <replay-id or hashed-prompt>, route, tenant, model_hint. Root span name: "request:<route>"
- Model span: name "model.call:<model_name>:<version>", tags: pool_id, gpu_index, kv_cache_hit=true/false, fanout_index if part of fanout.
- KV span: "kv.lookup:<store>" with tags key_sample (hashed), prefix_key_hit=true/false, prefetch=true/false.
- Enrichment: attach playback-replay-id and anonymized prompt-shard id only (never full prompt).
- Trace anchors: operator panels link to trace URL with query params: highlight span where kv.lookup.prefix_key_hit=false OR model.call with queue_latency > 50ms.

Example span ordering for a fanout request:
- request:chat-complete (root)
  - prompt-store.fetch (child)
  - kv.lookup:prefix (child)
  - model.call:llama-65b:1 (child)
    - gpu.exec (subspan)
  - model.call:reranker:1 (child)

Dashboard: minimal 6-panel view (layout rationale + queries)
1) UPL overview: p50/p90/p99 first-token latency by route (small heatmap). Rationale: immediate user impact.
2) Token latency decomposition: stacked quantiles for server.token_latency_ms broken by model and seq_len bucket. Rationale: detect long-tail token generation.
3) KV Warmth panel: pool-level kv.prefetch_hit_ratio time-series + alarm overlay. Rationale: cold-cache bursts often precede regressive tails.
4) Fanout and branch map: gauge of fanout.branch_count distribution and top fanout patterns (2+ calls). Rationale: captures spiky parallelism costs.
5) Pool queue + dequeue latency: 95th queue_latency_ms per pool with scatter of batch sizes. Rationale: shows contention and batching anomalies.
6) Trace-links and quick-actions: list of recent high-latency requests (p99 UPL) with 1-click link to trace + suggested hypothesis toggles ("show KV cold hits", "filter fanout>1").

Probes and synthetic checks (lightweight):
- KV probe (every 30s per region): issue a small prefix lookup, measure prefetch_hit and kv lookup latency. Report to kv.prefetch_hit_ratio.
- Warmup probe (on model deploy): run a 3-request sequence to prime KV and model caches and validate p90 token latency < target.
- Fanout probe (every 5m): synthetic request that forces 2 model calls to measure added overhead and validate detours.

Runbook snippet (3-minute operator flow):
1) Open panel 1 -> confirm UPL spike route(s).
2) Panel 2 + 5 -> check if server token latency skewed by long seq_len or queue latency.
3) Panel 3 -> if kv.prefetch_hit_ratio dropped, jump to traces filtering kv_lookup.prefix_key_hit=false.
4) Panel 4 -> if fanout>1, filter traces by fanout_index to inspect which branch adds latency.
5) Open trace from panel 6 and look for model.call queue_latency and gpu.exec durations.
6) If root cause unclear, escalate to serving-runtime oncall with trace id and top 3 suspected causes (kv-cold, pool-saturation, fanout-regression).

Open questions and unresolved decisions from workshop:
- Should we compute tenant-weighted SLOs or stick to pool-level SLOs? (Tentative: pool-level SLOs for now, add tenant-slices later.)
- How to represent bursty cold-cache scenarios from customers that have per-tenant prefix variability?
- Enforcement: add automatic trace tagger in the proxy to inject fanout_index and replay-id? (Action: prototype in proxy team).

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Aisha: Draft dashboard queries + SQL templates for the 6-panel view. ETA 2026-01-10.
- Miguel: Add probe implementation to telemetry repo (PR link included). ETA 2025-12-01.
- Bethany: Prototype trace anchor links and add to trace UI docs. ETA 2026-01-15.
- Noah: Run a 2-week shadow of panels and gather query cost metrics. ETA 2026-02-01.

Notes and heuristics (operators):
- When investigating p99 token spikes, always check kv.prefetch_hit_ratio and pool.queue_latency_ms before diving into model execution duration.
- Tagging: prefer enumerated boolean tags (kv_hit, fanout) over free-form strings to enable fast filtering.

Appendix: useful queries and snippets (inline):
- kv.prefetch_hit_ratio query (pseudo-SQL): SELECT region, pool, avg(kv_hit::int) as hit_ratio FROM kv_lookup WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '10 minutes' GROUP BY 1,2
- token latency quantiles (pseudo-SQL): SELECT model, percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY token_latency_ms) as p99 FROM token_latency WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '5 minutes' GROUP BY 1

End of notes.

Workshop attendees: Aisha, Miguel, Bethany, Noah, Priya Verma, Tomasz Kowalski, Serena Park.

Status: moving to dashboard prototype (Aisha) and probe PR (Miguel).
